questions.question: The Tripartite Struggle, also known as the Kannauj Triangle Wars, took place in the 8th and 9th centuries, between which of these three great Indian dynasties?
questions.option_1: The Cholas, The Pratiharas and The Rashtrakutas
questions.option_2: The Paramars, The Chauhans The Gahadavalas
questions.option_3: The Pandayas, The Pratiharas and The Rashtrakutas
questions.option_4: The Palas, The Pratiharas and The Rashtrakutas
questions.solution:
The Tripartite Struggle for control over Kannauj was fought between the Palas, Pratiharas, and Rashtrakutas.
  • Kannauj was considered a symbol of sovereignty in North India.
  • The struggle lasted for over two centuries.

questions.question: The formal British rule in India is understood to have commenced in 1757, after the Battle of ______.
questions.solution:
The formal British rule in India is considered to have started after the Battle of Plassey in 1757.
  • The British forces were led by Robert Clive against Nawab Siraj-ud-Daulah.
  • Mir Jafar's treachery played a key role in the British victory.

questions.question: The Communist Party of India was founded at ________ in October 1920.
questions.solution:
The Communist Party of India (CPI) was founded in Tashkent (Uzbekistan) in October 1920.
  • Key founders included M.N. Roy, Abani Mukherji, and others.
  • M.N. Roy was the first to propose the idea of a Constituent Assembly for India.

questions.question: Who among the following repealed the Vernacular Press Act of 1878?
questions.solution:
Lord Ripon repealed the Vernacular Press Act in 1882.
  • The Act was originally passed by Lord Lytton in 1878 to suppress local newspapers.
  • Ripon is known as the 'Father of Local Self-Government' in India.

questions.question: Who among the following was the commander of Muhammad Ghori, and also founded the slave dynasty in India?
questions.solution:
Qutub-ud-Din Aibak was the commander of Muhammad Ghori and founded the Slave (Mamluk) Dynasty in 1206.
  • He started the construction of the Qutub Minar in Delhi.
  • He was known as 'Lakh Baksh' for his generosity.

questions.question: Which of the following were NOT a part of a citadel in Harrapan architecture?
questions.solution:
In Harappan cities, the residential buildings for masses were located in the Lower Town, not the Citadel.
  • The Citadel contained important structures like the Great Bath, Granaries, and fire altars.
  • The Lower Town was usually larger and housed the common people.

questions.question: Which among the following Universities is founded by Pandit Madan Mohan Malaviya?
questions.solution:
Pandit Madan Mohan Malaviya founded the Banaras Hindu University (BHU) in 1916.
  • He was a four-time President of the Indian National Congress.
  • He was posthumously awarded the Bharat Ratna in 2014.

questions.question: Who is the author of ‘The Inheritance of Loss’?
questions.solution:
The novel 'The Inheritance of Loss' was written by Kiran Desai.
  • She won the Man Booker Prize for this book in 2006.
  • The story explores themes of colonialism and globalization.

questions.question: The claim for ‘swarajya’ or self-government within the British Empire, on the model of self-governing colonies like Australia and Canada, was put forward from the Congress platform in 1905 by:
questions.solution:
In the 1905 Banaras session, Gopal Krishna Gokhale put forward the claim for Swarajya (self-government).
  • Gokhale was a moderate leader and founder of the Servants of India Society.
  • He was the political guru of Mahatma Gandhi.

questions.question: In ______ the Mughal emperor appointed the Company as the Diwan of the provinces of Bengal.
questions.solution:
In 1765, the Mughal Emperor Shah Alam II granted the Diwani Rights of Bengal, Bihar, and Odisha to the East India Company.
  • This followed the British victory in the Battle of Buxar.
  • It allowed the British to collect taxes directly from these provinces.

questions.question: Which of the following war ended with the treaty of Salbai?
questions.solution:
The Treaty of Salbai (1782) ended the First Anglo-Maratha War.
  • It was signed between the Marathas and the British East India Company.
  • It ensured peace between the two powers for twenty years.

questions.question: In which of the following years Sikandar Lodi founded Agra?
questions.solution:
Sikandar Lodi founded the city of Agra in 1504 CE.
  • He shifted the capital from Delhi to Agra in 1506.
  • He was the most powerful ruler of the Lodi Dynasty.

questions.question: In 1856, Governor-General ______ decided that Bahadur Shah Zafar would be the last Mughal king and after his death none of his descendants would be recognised as kings - they would just be called princes.
questions.solution:
In 1856, Lord Canning announced that Bahadur Shah Zafar would be the last Mughal King.
  • Canning was the Governor-General during the Revolt of 1857.
  • Zafar was later exiled to Rangoon (Burma) where he died in 1862.

questions.question: In the third karnatak war, the British East India Company defeated the French forces at the ______ in 1760 ending almost a century of conflict over French supremacy in India.
questions.solution:
The British defeated the French in the Battle of Wandiwash in 1760.
  • This battle was part of the Third Carnatic War.
  • The British forces were led by Sir Eyre Coote, while the French were led by Comte de Lally.

questions.question: The Dahsala system under the administration of Akbar was related to:
questions.solution:
The Dahsala System (also known as the Todar Mal's Bandobast) was a land revenue system under Akbar.
  • Revenue was calculated based on the average produce and prices of the last ten years.
  • Raja Todar Mal was Akbar's finance minister.

questions.question: In Delhi sultanate, the Bandagan were known as ____________.
questions.option_1: special slaves purchased for military service
questions.option_2: special officers for collecting land revenue
questions.option_3: special artisans deployed in royal Kharkhanas
questions.option_4: special persons appointed for religious conversion
questions.solution:
In the Delhi Sultanate, Bandagan were special slaves purchased for military service.
  • They were highly trained and often promoted to high political offices.
  • The system was particularly prominent during the reign of Iltutmish.

questions.question: Lord Dalhousie, the Governor-General, introduced which of the following policies pertaining to the expansion of the British Empire?
questions.solution:
Lord Dalhousie introduced the Doctrine of Lapse to expand the British Empire.
  • Under this policy, if an Indian ruler died without a male heir, the state would 'lapse' to the British.
  • Satara was the first state to be annexed (1848) under this policy.

questions.question: In which of these battles the involvement of the Mughal army was not there?
questions.solution:
The Battle of Aliwal (1846) was fought between the British and the Sikh Empire; hence the Mughal army was not involved.
  • The Mughal army was involved in Panipat II, Buxar (Shah Alam II), and Haldighati (Akbar).
  • Aliwal was a key battle in the First Anglo-Sikh War.

questions.question: The ‘Surat Split’ took place in the session of the Indian National Congress in the year _________.
questions.solution:
The 'Surat Split' of the Indian National Congress occurred in 1907.
  • The conflict was between the Extremists (Lal-Bal-Pal) and the Moderates.
  • The Extremists wanted Lala Lajpat Rai or Tilak as President, while Moderates chose Rash Behari Ghosh.

questions.question: In south, who was the founder of the dynasty called Rashtrakuta dynasty?
questions.solution:
The Rashtrakuta Dynasty was founded by Dantidurga in the mid-8th century.
  • Their capital was located at Manyakheta (Karnataka).
  • They are famous for building the Kailasa Temple at Ellora.

questions.question: Who founded the Asiatic Society of Bengal in 1784?
questions.solution:
The Asiatic Society of Bengal was founded in 1784 by Sir William Jones.
  • He was a linguist and a judge at the Supreme Court in Calcutta.
  • The society published the famous journal 'Asiatick Researches'.

questions.question: Who founded the city of Agra?
questions.solution:
The city of Agra was founded by Sikandar Lodi in 1504.
  • Agra served as the capital for several Mughal emperors, including Akbar and Shah Jahan.
  • Sikandar Lodi also introduced the Gazz-i-Sikandari for land measurement.

questions.question: Which Bahmani ruler granted the title of ‘Chief of the Merchants’ or Malikut-Tujjar to Mahmud Gawan?
questions.solution:
The Bahmani Sultan Humayun Shah granted the title of Malikut-Tujjar (Chief of Merchants) to Mahmud Gawan.
  • Mahmud Gawan was a brilliant administrator and Persian merchant.
  • He served as the Prime Minister (Peshwa) of the Bahmani kingdom.

questions.question: In which of the following battles, did the founder of the Mughal Empire, Babur, use cannon and ammunition effectively for the first time in India?
questions.solution:
Babur used cannons and gunpowder effectively for the first time in India during the First Battle of Panipat (1526).
  • He defeated the larger army of Ibrahim Lodi using the Tulghuma and Araba tactics.
  • This battle marked the beginning of the Mughal Empire in India.

questions.question: The Anushilan Samiti was active in which part of the Indian subcontinent in the 20th century?
questions.solution:
The Anushilan Samiti was a prominent revolutionary organization active in Bengal.
  • It was founded by Pramathanath Mitra and Aurobindo Ghosh.
  • It aimed to end British rule through revolutionary violence.
